videos.script: In lesson 4, ana's password leaked, and it opened her payslip from the other side of the internet. {{lesson4}} A password is something you know. Anything you know can be copied, guessed or typed into the wrong page. {{know}} A second factor asks for something of a different kind. Something you have, like a phone. Or something you are, like a fingerprint. {{factors}} You will watch a six-digit code being made from a secret and the clock. The phone and the server compute it apart, and they agree. {{code}} Then the uncomfortable part. Not every second factor stops the same attacks. Some can be phished, some can be worn down. And the way back in for somebody who lost their phone is often the weakest door of all. {{weak}}
